title: Workspaces orphaned by a stale id: Dispose must reclaim by identity, not by bookkeeping
description:
Workspaces survive their tick and become unreachable: the tick is CLOSED, the
manifest that named the workspace is GONE, the workspace and its git worktree
are still live, and the workspace's tick tokens are missing — so nothing can
find it by tick id ever again. Only a human reading a sidebar notices.

Observed 2026-09-10 in the canonify repo (a different epic, same substrate):
workspaces wP5 j5s, wP6 0i9, wP7 226, wP8 hf1, wP9 3i5, wPA 15e, wPB fw3 all
alive with worktrees under ~/.herdr/worktrees/canonify/tick-*, all with
`tokens: {}` in `herdr workspace list`, all with their tick CLOSED and NO
manifest under `.tick/logs/herd/*/`. The one workspace that still carries
`TICK=we9` is the one whose tick is still in_progress.

ticks' own cleanup is careful and is probably NOT the bug: it removes the
manifest LAST so an incomplete teardown is retryable, it re-checks liveness next
to the destructive step rather than at run start, and it refuses when herdr will
not answer. Two of its behaviours combine badly with a herdr RESTART, which is
the likely trigger — herdr went 0.8.2 to 0.9.0 (protocol 20 to 22) in this
window:

1. `planFor` notes "manifest records no workspace id — nothing to remove in
   herdr" and proceeds to remove the manifest anyway.
2. `apply` treats `workspace_not_found` from worktree.remove as SUCCESS — which
   is right when the workspace is genuinely gone, and wrong when the id in the
   manifest is merely STALE. Either way the manifest is then removed, and the
   real workspace, now under an id nothing records, is unreachable.

Workspace tokens are herdr-side metadata (set through pane/workspace
report_metadata), so a restart that loses them removes the last independent way
to re-derive the mapping.

## Why this belongs in Phase 2

ticfac's executor owns Dispose, and Phase 1 already established the two
principles this needs. Attempts are ADOPTED BY TICK ID rather than by a
remembered handle, and the reconciler PRUNES missing worktrees at startup. The
herdr executor must do the equivalent for workspaces, or the same leak arrives
in ticfac with the same shape.

Do:
- Dispose must be idempotent AND identity-based: given a tick and an attempt it
  must be able to find the workspace even when the recorded id is stale, by
  asking herdr what exists rather than trusting bookkeeping. A workspace whose
  worktree path names the tick is evidence; so is a branch.
- Do NOT treat `workspace_not_found` as proof of teardown when the id could be
  stale. Distinguish "this workspace is gone" from "this id is unknown", and
  refuse rather than record success on the second — the same fail-closed rule
  tick x6j applies to substrate answers generally.
- Reclamation at startup: a run should be able to list herdr workspaces whose
  tick belongs to this epic and whose tick is CLOSED, and report them. Removal
  is destructive, so report first; only remove what the operator or a declared
  policy authorises.
- Record the workspace id in provenance alongside the herdr protocol and server
  version (tick d9m), so a stale id can be recognised as stale rather than
  guessed at.

Note the interaction with resume-across-an-upgrade, which d9m and x6j already
own: this is the same hazard seen from the disposal end rather than the dispatch
end. A herdr restart is exactly when both bite.
acceptance_criteria: Dispose finds and tears down a workspace whose recorded id is stale, by asking herdr what exists rather than trusting the manifest; a test drives disposal against a changed workspace id and asserts the workspace is actually gone. workspace_not_found is no longer recorded as successful teardown when the id may be stale: 'this workspace is gone' and 'this id is unknown' are distinguishable and the second refuses. A run can list and report herdr workspaces belonging to this epic whose tick is closed, without removing anything unless authorised. The workspace id is recorded in provenance alongside the herdr protocol and server version. go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green (make test-short).
